title: PVFormer: Proper Velocity Transformer for Stable and Scalable Hyperbolic Representation Learning
claim: Several common geometric models describe the same space, but one is unconstrained and so is simpler to work in.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, isometry symbols between panels, matching 2-D point sketches
description: Three rounded panels sit side by side. Each is titled with a model name and gives its set definition in math. The left panel, Poincaré ball, shows a light-blue disk with a bold blue boundary and four blue points inside. The middle panel, Lorentz model, shows a purple one-sheeted hyperboloid or cone with a wireframe, three axes and three purple points. The right panel, Proper velocity, shows a plain 2-D coordinate plane with green points scattered across it and no boundary. Between the panels the word 'isometry' appears above a ≅ symbol, showing the models are equivalent. The colors differ for each panel (blue, purple, green). The eye goes first to the bounded disk on the left and then to the open axes on the right.
caption: Comparison of three two-dimensional hyperbolic models. PV represents the same hyperbolic geometry as the Poincaré and Lorentz models, but removes equality or inequality constraints.
abstract: Hyperbolic representations have shown remarkable success on hierarchical and tree-like data, and Transformers have become a central architecture for representation learning. However, a principled construction of hyperbolic Transformers remains challenging because the self-attention layer decomposes into three coupled primitives, transformation, similarity, and aggregation, that should all respect the underlying geometry. Existing hyperbolic Transformer designs are typically built in the PoincarÃ© or Lorentz models, where bounded domains, time-like constraints, tangent-space detours, or projection steps make it difficult to keep the full block intrinsic and scalable. To address this gap, we propose PVFormer, to the best of our knowledge, the first Transformer architecture that operates natively in proper velocity (PV) space. The proper velocity model provides an unconstrained representation of hyperbolic geometry, and PVFormer exploits this structure to redesign the Transformer block in PV space. On the transformation side, we use PV homomorphism transformations to update query and value representations. On the similarity side, we generalize Euclidean inner-product attention with a PV Busemann score inspired by Busemann-based hyperbolic learning and a PV point-to-hyperplane key transformation. On the aggregation side, we replace Euclidean averaging with PV midpoint aggregation and further derive a scalable PV linear attention variant for large graphs. Extensive experiments support the effectiveness of PVFormer across graph, text, and vision benchmarks.
